FROMLIST:ath10k: Add the adjacent wlan radio interference detecting interface Some platforms integrate several radios together. When one radio wants to spectral scan the currently channel, the adjacent radio's activity will introduce some interference in the spectral scan result. To combat the problem, enable the FW to set a special mark within the spectral scan results. Using such a mark the user who is processing the data can identify whether the data has been introduced to interference by the adjacent radio during that period. The user can interpret more accurate spectral scan results given marks where interference occurred. This technique requires the preconditions that the scanning and adjacent radio have some physical connection to make them aware of each other's activity from within the FW layer, and the FW claimed supporting this capability. BUG=chrome-os-partner:38286 TEST=build/boot on storm succeeded, to enable this feature, execute: echo 1 > /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phyX/ath10k/adjacent_wlan_interfrc Then run the spectral scan steps. ... To check whether the spectral scan data be interfered, execute: cat /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phyX/ath10k/adjacent_wlan_interfrc INTERFRC DETECT FOR SPEC SCAN: Enable/Disable 5G_interference: X/0 2G_Interference: X/0 X means the interference number in the scan period, 0 means no interference. These counters will be reset when next round spectral scan be triggered Signed-off-by: Yanbo Li <yanbol@qca.qualcomm.com> (cherry picked from commit fa8f5266b571475c56a22d702bba9a6a0ed5c015) (source: wireless-3.18) Signed-off-by: Ashok Raj Nagarajan <arnagara@codeaurora.org> Change-Id: I0815c7e6e0a540ecc31cac820d7755e43c3ae7be Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/310156 Commit-Ready: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Tested-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

FROMLIST:ath10k: Ignore the adjacent radio's activity when surveying a channel The overall goal for a scanning radio is to evaluate the outside radio environment. Some platforms integrate several radios together. When one radio wants to survey the current channel, the adjacent radio's activity will make this survey result inaccurate. the switcher can be used to enable the FW to ignore the survey time slot when the adjacent radio is active, especially for TX. This skipped scan approach will make the survey result more accurate. This technique requires a precondition that the scanning and adjacent radio have some physical connection to make them aware of each other's activity from within the FW layer, and the FW claimed supporting this capability. BUG=chrome-os-partner:40009 TEST=build/boot on storm succeeded, to enable this feature, execute: echo 2 > /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phyX/ath10k/adjacent_wlan_interfrc Then run the survey scan and dump the stastics: iw dev wifiX survey dump The TX&RX counter showed already deducted the time slot be interfered To check whether the feature is enabled, execute: cat /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phyX/ath10k/adjacent_wlan_interfrc INTERFRC DETECT FOR SURVEY SCAN: Enable/Disable Signed-off-by: Yanbo Li <yanbol@qca.qualcomm.com> (cherry picked from commit 18c00f35844dae539c33f058d5e50ab3d1858221) (source: wireless-3.18) Change-Id: Ia152ff1a24fbf441702ce1ec87f38e21efd68ae9 Signed-off-by: Ashok Raj Nagarajan <arnagara@codeaurora.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/310157 Commit-Ready: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Tested-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

ath10k: Supply the 64bits channel survey counters The previous TX&RX cycle counters used to report the channel survey are 32 bits, it will wraparound after reach 0xffffffff, the wraparound happens in a short cycle (24 seconds), if the user want survey >24 seconds TX&RX counters on a specific channel, the counters will overflow again and again which make the long time survey impossible. There is a new WMI message be added to access the counter in 64bits format, it will greatly extent the overflow time, and userspace will have enough time to handle such case by calculate the counter difference between two samples. The userspace application could call the NL80211_CMD_GET_SURVEY to get the 64 bits counter survey result of currently channel, the result also can be gotten via the available command "iw station survey dump" known limitation: 1: Not be tested for multichannel support scenario 2: Background scan at hostapd AP mode need verificaiton BUG=chrome-os-partner:38165 TEST=build/boot on storm succeeded, The userspace application could call the NL80211_CMD_GET_SURVEY to get the 64 bits counter survey result of currently channel, the result also can be gotten via the available command "iw station survey dump" Signed-off-by: Yanbo Li <yanbol@qca.qualcomm.com> (cherry picked from commit 3be4c4565684111071c2dd7121896451c714b45a) (source: wireless-3.18) Change-Id: I5ee22e837b14d360b5f3577f4c8dd2e8fbfcf4a2 Signed-off-by: Ashok Raj Nagarajan <arnagara@codeaurora.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/310158 Commit-Ready: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Tested-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: kasan: fix last shadow judgement in ... ... memory_is_poisoned_16() The shadow which correspond 16 bytes memory may span 2 or 3 bytes. If the memory is aligned on 8, then the shadow takes only 2 bytes. So we check "shadow_first_bytes" is enough, and need not to call "memory_is_poisoned_1(addr + 15);". But the code "if (likely(!last_byte))" is wrong judgement. e.g. addr=0, so last_byte = 15 & KASAN_SHADOW_MASK = 7, then the code will continue to call "memory_is_poisoned_1(addr + 15);" Signed-off-by: Xishi Qiu <qiuxishi@huawei.com> Acked-by: Andrey Ryabinin <aryabinin@virtuozzo.com> Cc: Andrey Konovalov <adech.fo@gmail.com> Cc: Rusty Russell <rusty@rustcorp.com.au> Cc: Michal Marek <mmarek@suse.cz> Cc: <zhongjiang@huawei.com> Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org> Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org> (cherry picked from commit 8d77a6d18ae9ccfd5eee1cc551ee4ac27fd41464) Signed-off-by: Alexander Potapenko <glider@google.com> BUG=chromium:545468 TEST=KASAN reports on `modprobe test_kasan` Change-Id: I90af4cfb6e3b4f37b4703e8a52667f37c326c236 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/307976 Commit-Ready: Alexander Potapenko <glider@chromium.org> Tested-by: Alexander Potapenko <glider@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Olof Johansson <olofj@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: x86, efi, kasan: #undef memset/memcpy/memmove per arch In not-instrumented code KASAN replaces instrumented memset/memcpy/memmove with not-instrumented analogues __memset/__memcpy/__memove. However, on x86 the EFI stub is not linked with the kernel. It uses not-instrumented mem*() functions from arch/x86/boot/compressed/string.c So we don't replace them with __mem*() variants in EFI stub. On ARM64 the EFI stub is linked with the kernel, so we should replace mem*() functions with __mem*(), because the EFI stub runs before KASAN sets up early shadow. So let's move these #undef mem* into arch's asm/efi.h which is also included by the EFI stub. Also, this will fix the warning in 32-bit build reported by kbuild test robot: efi-stub-helper.c:599:2: warning: implicit declaration of function 'memcpy' [akpm@linux-foundation.org: use 80 cols in comment] Signed-off-by: Andrey Ryabinin <ryabinin.a.a@gmail.com> Reported-by: Fengguang Wu <fengguang.wu@gmail.com> Cc: Will Deacon <will.deacon@arm.com> Cc: Catalin Marinas <catalin.marinas@arm.com> Cc: Matt Fleming <matt.fleming@intel.com> Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de> Cc: Ingo Molnar <mingo@redhat.com> Cc: "H. CHROMIUM: soc/tegra: fix the BPMP connection failure Currently we try to connect to BPMP right after the FW was just loaded on it, but the BPMP needs some boot time to make the connection success. So we fix this by adding some tolerance time for the BPMP bring up before the first connection to BPMP. BUG=chrome-os-partner:47358 TEST=reboot stress test and no error messages below can be observed tegra-bpmp-mailman 6000f200.bpmp-mailman: Unable to startup the chan (-19) tegra-bpmp-mailman 6000f200.bpmp-mailman: failed to request mailbox: -19 Change-Id: Iad4e218762064c544b284dad7dea57a9b1806a0e Signed-off-by: Joseph Lo <josephl@nvidia.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/311303 Commit-Ready: Andrew Bresticker <abrestic@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrew Bresticker <abrestic@chromium.org>
